planting.note: Divide rhizomes or plant tissue-culture starts in moist, nutrient-poor, acidic medium (50/50 peat moss and perlite) in full sun; water only with rain water or distilled water. B52 requires a winter dormancy period (50°F for 3-4 months).

directions: Grow in a mix of 50% peat moss and 50% perlite or sand (no potting soil, no fertilizer), keep the medium wet using rain water or distilled water only, and provide maximum sun. B52 is a large-clone Venus flytrap cultivar bred and selected for exceptionally large trap size, among the biggest of any named flytrap cultivar, with mature traps noticeably larger than the wild-type species while retaining the same fast, hair-triggered snap closure. Its bigger traps make it a favorite for growers who want a more dramatic specimen or who feed their plants insects, since larger traps can process larger prey. Like other flytraps it needs a cold winter dormancy of 3-4 months at around 50°F to remain healthy long-term, and the most common causes of failure are tap water, fertilizer, and insufficient sun.

planting.note: Divide rhizomes or plant tissue-culture starts in moist, nutrient-poor, acidic medium (50/50 peat moss and perlite) in full sun; water only with rain water or distilled water. Red Dragon needs strong, direct sun to develop its deepest red coloring.

directions: Grow in a mix of 50% peat moss and 50% perlite or sand (no potting soil, no fertilizer), keep the medium wet using rain water or distilled water only, and provide maximum sun. Red Dragon is one of the most popular Venus flytrap cultivars for its entirely deep burgundy-red coloring across both the leaves and the toothed trap interiors, rather than the green leaves with only red-tinged trap linings typical of the wild species; the color intensifies to its darkest, most saturated red with strong, direct sunlight. Like other flytraps it needs a cold winter dormancy of 3-4 months at around 50°F to remain healthy long-term, and insufficient light is the most common reason a Red Dragon fails to develop its signature deep color, often reverting toward green in shade.

common_name: Dentate Traps Venus Flytrap (Short Shark-Tooth Cultivar)

planting.note: Divide rhizomes or plant tissue-culture starts in moist, nutrient-poor, acidic medium (50/50 peat moss and perlite) in full sun; water only with rain water or distilled water. Dentate Traps requires a winter dormancy period (50°F for 3-4 months).

directions: Grow in a mix of 50% peat moss and 50% perlite or sand (no potting soil, no fertilizer), keep the medium wet using rain water or distilled water only, and provide maximum sun. Dentate Traps is a novelty Venus flytrap cultivar with unusually short, stubby, blunt marginal teeth in place of the long, thin, hair-like cilia of the wild species, giving the trap edges a distinctly toothy, jagged, shark-jaw appearance rather than the delicate interlocking fringe typical of most flytraps. The traps themselves are otherwise fully functional, closing and digesting prey normally despite the unusual tooth shape. Like other flytraps it needs a cold winter dormancy of 3-4 months at around 50°F to remain healthy long-term, and the most common causes of failure are tap water, fertilizer, and insufficient sun.
